title: Floyd's gold orchestra, C.G. Conn horn and Floyd as leader
summary: Floyd's orchestra had gold instruments; Albert was given a trumpet and rehearsals were frequent; Floyd had faults but was a nice man.

bands.name: Troy Floyd and his Orchestra of Gold

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yes, he's dead now. That's right. Were these, you'd say Troy Floyd's band was a happy band, or they were all happy together?

Right, right. The name of the band was Troy Floyd and his orchestra of gold. Everybody had gold instruments. And I never, I should have kept this, but I don't know why I didn't. C.G. Kahn made me a present of the first long trumpet that was made. And they carried my name on the little pamphlets in my picture, showing that I blew nothing but C.G. Kahn instruments. I never did keep this. I should have. Do you still play Kahn? No, I'm not playing a Selma. But I have nothing against C.G. Kahn. I think it's a tremendous instrument.
Say you were going to meet up with them back at the Battle of New. Say you were going to meet up with somebody, would you rehearse before you met?
No, you just go play your regular O-T music. Just like you play everyone. It was just a gimmick to bring the people in.

Did Troy Floyd's band rehearse much? Quite a bit. Quite a bit of rehearsals. Every day or a week? Two or three times a week. And what kind of leader was Floyd? Was he a good salesman? What about being on the stand?

Well, the fella's dead man. You know, you don't talk about a dead man. All in all, Troy was, to me, was a nice fella. Had some bad faults that a band leader shouldn't have had. What I imagined in those days, what he did was just normal reaction to a man that became partly famous. We had our differences.
